mbm-0093.clue: I run with a square of yellow cloth.
mbm-0093.quote: My daughter makes a finish line between the gateposts with her scarf. The first time I got there early she made me go round the block until she had it tied.

mbm-0094.clue: The blue corner used to catch the wind.
mbm-0094.quote: Our old kite split along the crosspiece. I sewed the sail into a quilt for the couch. There’s just enough tail left to tickle your ankle when you lie down.

mbm-0095.clue: Our picnic quilt has one strawberry in the corner.
mbm-0095.quote: My niece lifted the edge of my new quilt and found a wild strawberry underneath. I stitched one in that corner when we got home. She checks underneath it every time.

mbm-0096.clue: I can hear which mat I’m standing on.
mbm-0096.quote: One floorboard in our practice hall gives a little squeak when I shift my weight. My instructor closes her eyes and listens for it. I haven’t fooled her yet.

mbm-0097.clue: The kettle sings a B flat.
mbm-0097.quote: I was learning a duet and couldn’t find anybody home to start my part. The kettle whistled exactly on cue. These days I make tea before rehearsal.

mbm-0098.clue: We make one the size of a coin.
mbm-0098.quote: My smallest arepa is a tester for the pan. My granny puts a tiny pat of butter on it with a toothpick, sets out her smallest saucer and calls it the chef’s breakfast.

mbm-0099.clue: I repair the flag before I putt.
mbm-0099.quote: A moth made a hole in the little flag on our practice green. I patched it with a yellow sun. It’s the one hole where I can honestly say I aim for the sun.

mbm-0100.quote: I leaned across a wet bowl in my cable-knit sweater. The print stayed when it fired. My mum uses it for soup and says her hands know it’s mine.

mbm-0101.clue: Two left shoes got me through the door.
mbm-0101.quote: The lights were out when I packed for dance night. My friend loaned me a right sneaker in the coatroom. In the photo our feet match, just in the wrong pairs.

mbm-0102.clue: I have a whole cassette of ten-second songs.
mbm-0102.quote: The DJ let me tape the bit between one record and the next. I practice those tiny transitions in our hall. When the music changes I already know where my foot goes.

mbm-0103.clue: Feel the little ridge along the border.
mbm-0103.quote: My granddad’s tape measure snapped last spring. I used the cloth sleeve it lived in to bind the end of a quilt. Somehow he still checks my corners with his fingers.

mbm-0104.clue: I’m saving the ending for a bench.
mbm-0104.quote: I read that sea adventure one chapter at a time on the ferry. I missed the last crossing before the harbor froze, so I sat on the dock to finish it with the right soundtrack.

mbm-0105.clue: There are two ways to look at the rooster.
mbm-0105.quote: I stitched a rooster upside down in my neighbor’s kitchen quilt. We finally found a way to turn him right side up. You have to open the cold oven door and hold him over the handle. He's a lot of work for a chicken.

mbm-0106.clue: My scorecard has a wet circle on seven.
mbm-0106.quote: That’s where Dad set his lemonade to free both hands and clap. I made a long putt and wrote the score inside the ring. He still frames it with his glass whenever he tells the story.

mbm-0107.clue: I keep one negative in a matchbox.
mbm-0107.quote: I photographed a family picnic through the hole in the handle of our soup ladle. Everybody is framed in a perfect silver circle. I still bring it to reunions.

mbm-0108.clue: The cuff is also a map.
mbm-0108.quote: I embroidered the bend in the river onto a shirt for my brother. He rolls the cuff up when we pass our old swimming spot, like he’s checking our position.

mbm-0109.clue: I have a book that shuts itself.
mbm-0109.quote: The cover is so warped I hold it open with a lemon on each side. I finished the last chapter in the kitchen and made lemonade before I told anyone how it ended.

mbm-0110.clue: The bus engine gives me the first note.
mbm-0110.quote: Our choir rehearses above the depot. We used to wait for the buses to go. Now our bass singer catches the engine note and we all come in before the doors close.

mbm-0111.clue: I bring two clothespins to the beach.
mbm-0111.quote: I clip my hat to the back of the deckchair because I always fall asleep in the sun. Last time I woke up underneath a row of tiny socks my niece had hung there to dry.

mbm-0112.clue: The quietest place is under the old bridge.
mbm-0112.quote: I raised one paddle blade there and let the water drip. Each drop hit the river twice, once for real and once from the arch. I stayed until the blade was dry.

mbm-0113.quote: On my first trip alone I found a bronze fish cast into a drain cover. Now I can tell six towns apart just by the little pictures under my shoes.

mbm-0114.clue: I still have the cardboard steering wheel.
mbm-0114.quote: My sister wanted to race me on the console before she could work the buttons. I cut her a wheel from a cereal box. She steered and I pressed, and she still claims our record.

mbm-0115.clue: I carry an extra dry sock on the river.
mbm-0115.quote: At the takeout we found a tiny frog in my spare sock. We turned the cuff down and let it hop straight onto a lily pad. First passenger I’ve ever dropped at its front door.

mbm-0116.clue: I have a card nobody can shuffle.
mbm-0116.quote: I painted a giant copy of my friend’s favorite forest troll on cardboard for her birthday. At game night it occupies a whole folding chair and still has terrible defense.

mbm-0117.clue: The same train has two voices.
mbm-0117.quote: I sit where the railway comes out of a short tunnel. The whistle goes low inside and bright outside. I keep drawing two little notes beside the engine number.
